questions.prompt: A \(2.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) cart moving at \(3.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) sticks to a \(1.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) cart at rest. Find the common speed.
An isolated object initially at rest splits into two pieces. One piece has momentum \(5\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the other piece's momentum.
questions.answer:
Initial total momentum is zero, so the other piece has
\[
\vec{p}_2=-5\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A \(0.010\,\mathrm{kg}\) pellet leaves a \(4.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) launcher at \(400\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the launcher's recoil speed, assuming the system starts at rest.
questions.answer:
Initial momentum is zero:
\[
0=0.010(400)+4.0v
\]
\[
v=-1.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The launcher recoils opposite the pellet.

questions.prompt: Two objects have momenta \(3\hat{\imath}+4\hat{\jmath}\) and \(-\hat{\imath}+2\hat{\jmath}\), in \(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}\). Find total momentum and its magnitude.
A \(60\,\mathrm{kg}\) skater at rest throws a \(5.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) package forward at \(6.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the skater's recoil speed.
questions.answer:
Forward package momentum is
\[
p=5.0(6.0)=30\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The skater has momentum \(-30\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}\), so
\[
v=\frac{-30}{60}=-0.50\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A \(4.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) system initially has total momentum \(10\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}\). An external impulse \(-6\hat{\imath}\,\mathrm{N\,s}\) acts. Find the final center-of-mass velocity.

Two carts at rest push apart on a frictionless track. Cart A has mass \(2.0\,\mathrm{kg}\), cart B has mass \(5.0\,\mathrm{kg}\), and cart A moves left at \(4.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find cart B's velocity and explain why total momentum is conserved.
questions.answer:
Take right as positive. Initial momentum is zero:
\[
2.0(-4.0)+5.0v_B=0
\]
\[
v_B=1.6\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]
Total momentum is conserved because the push forces are internal to the two-cart system and horizontal external impulse is negligible.

questions.prompt: A \(1.5\,\mathrm{kg}\) object moving east at \(8.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) explodes into two fragments. A \(0.50\,\mathrm{kg}\) fragment moves north at \(6.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the velocity vector of the other fragment.
questions.answer:
Initial momentum is
\[
\vec{P}_i=1.5(8.0)\hat{\imath}=12\hat{\imath}
\]
The north-moving fragment has
\[
\vec{p}_1=0.50(6.0)\hat{\jmath}=3\hat{\jmath}
\]
The other fragment has mass \(1.0\,\mathrm{kg}\), so
\[
\vec{p}_2=12\hat{\imath}-3\hat{\jmath}
\]
\[
\vec{v}_2=12\hat{\imath}-3\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A moving shell of mass \(6.0\,\mathrm{kg}\) travels east at \(12\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and explodes into three fragments. Two fragments have momenta \(20\hat{\imath}+15\hat{\jmath}\) and \(18\hat{\imath}-9\hat{\jmath}\), in \(\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the third fragment's momentum. State the isolation assumption and interpret the transverse components.
questions.answer:
Assume the explosion is short enough that external impulse is negligible. Initial momentum is
\[
\vec{P}_i=6.0(12)\hat{\imath}=72\hat{\imath}
\]
Thus
\[
\vec{p}_3=72\hat{\imath}-(20\hat{\imath}+15\hat{\jmath})-(18\hat{\imath}-9\hat{\jmath})
\]
\[
\vec{p}_3=34\hat{\imath}-6\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}
\]
The transverse components must sum to zero because the shell initially had no transverse momentum.

questions.prompt: An isolated object of mass \(M\) moves with speed \(V\) in the \(x\)-direction and breaks into masses \(\alpha M\) and \((1-\alpha)M\), where \(0<\alpha<1\). The first fragment moves perpendicular to the original direction with speed \(u\). Derive the second fragment's velocity components and the extra kinetic energy created by the breakup. State assumptions.
questions.answer:
Assume the breakup is isolated and nonrelativistic. Initial momentum is
\[
\vec{P}_i=MV\hat{\imath}
\]
The first fragment has momentum
\[
\vec{p}_1=\alpha M u\hat{\jmath}
\]
so the second fragment has
\[
\vec{p}_2=MV\hat{\imath}-\alpha M u\hat{\jmath}
\]
and
\[
\vec{v}_2=\frac{V}{1-\alpha}\hat{\imath}-\frac{\alpha u}{1-\alpha}\hat{\jmath}
\]
The kinetic energy increase is
\[
\Delta K=\frac{M\alpha}{2(1-\alpha)}(V^2+u^2)
\]
Interpretation: the breakup mechanism must supply this extra kinetic energy while internal impulses keep total momentum fixed.
